question: A merchant fixes the marked price of his goods at 60% above the cost price. He sells his goods at 25% discount. His percentage of profit is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We can use the successive percentage formula to find the overall effect: Net Profit % = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, markup a = +60% and discount b = −25%.

⇒ Net Profit % = 60 − 25 + [60 × (−25)] ÷ 100

⇒ Net Profit % = 35 − 1500 ÷ 100

⇒ Net Profit % = 35 − 15 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = 60% above Cost Price (CP)

Discount = 25% on MP

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 Profit and Discount Relationship
 CP → MP → SP
 
 
 CP: 100
 
 
 MP: 160
 
 
 SP: 120
 
 
• 
 

 +60% Markup
 
 
• 
 

 −25% Discount
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 

 +20% Profit

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the goods be 100 units.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 60% of 100 = 160

⇒ Discount = 25% of 160 = (25 ÷ 100) × 160 = 40

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount = 160 − 40 = 120

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 120 − 100 = 20

⇒ Profit% = (20 ÷ 100) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount Relation

Discount is always calculated strictly on the Marked Price (MP), not on Cost Price (CP). The final transaction price is Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount.

Successive Discount

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount can be calculated using the formula: [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

If a merchant sells goods at CP but uses a false weight, the actual Profit % is calculated as: [Error ÷ (True Weight − Error)] × 100.
